- **30×30 grid** rendered on a canvas, with the snake moving continuously in one of four directions
- **Classic rules** — eating food grows the snake and spawns new food; hitting a wall or itself ends the game
- **Keyboard controls** — Player 1 uses Arrow keys (or WASD), Player 2 uses WASD in two-human mode; keypress also restarts from the game-over screen
- **CPU-controlled snake** — an AI that pathfinds toward the food each tick while avoiding walls, its own body, and the other snake, with a survival fallback when the direct path is blocked

  2. CPU vs Human
  3. CPU vs CPU (demo/watch mode)

- **Restart with a keypress** (Enter/Space) from the game over screen, or return to the menu

Open the file in any browser to play.

{"edit_description":"Create a NEW complete, self-contained classic Snake game in this single HTML file — all CSS in one <style> block in <head>, all JS in one <script> block at the end of <body>, no external resources or libraries. It must fully work by just opening the file in a browser.

== GRID & RENDERING ==
- 30x30 grid on a <canvas> of 600x600 px (20px cells), subtle darker grid lines, dark theme page, everything centered.
- Two snakes on the same board: Snake 1 rendered green, Snake 2 rendered orange/cyan; heads drawn slightly brighter/with eyes; food drawn as a red apple-like square/circle.
- HUD above the canvas always visible during play: color-coded live scores "P1: N" and "P2: N" (label a CPU-controlled snake as "CPU"), the current mode name, and a small hint line ("Arrows/WASD move · P pause · R restart").

== CORE MECHANICS ==
- Fixed-tick game loop (~110 ms per step, optionally speeding up slightly as snakes grow, min ~70 ms).
- Each snake moves continuously in its current direction (up/down/left/right). At most one direction change applied per tick; 180-degree reversals must be ignored (use an input queue or last-applied-direction check).
- Food spawns on a random cell not occupied by any snake; keep at least 1 food on the board in all modes, 2 in versus modes.
- Eating food: snake grows by 1 segment (tail not removed that tick) and its score increments by 1.
- Death: a snake dies if its head goes outside the 30x30 grid (wall) or lands on any occupied body cell — its own body OR the opponent's body. Moving into the cell the opponent's tail vacates on the same tick is allowed (unless the opponent ate that tick). Head-to-head (both heads enter the same cell, or heads swap cells) kills BOTH snakes.
- The game ends as soon as at least one snake is dead: survivor wins; both dead on the same tick = draw.

== CONTROLS ==
- Player 1: Arrow keys. Player 2: W/A/S/D. Prevent default scrolling on these keys.
- Start menu: key "1" = Human vs Human, "2" = CPU vs Human (human controls Snake 1 with arrows, CPU controls Snake 2), "3" = CPU vs CPU. The three menu buttons must also be clickable with the mouse.
- During gameplay: "P" toggles pause (show a small "PAUSED" indicator).
- Game over screen: "R" (also Enter/Space) immediately restarts the same mode; "M" (or Esc) returns to the start menu. "R" also restarts the current mode mid-game.

== CPU AI (for any CPU-controlled snake) ==
- Every tick compute the move with BFS shortest path from the snake's head to the nearest food over the grid, treating walls and all snake body cells as obstacles (the opponent's tail cell may be treated as free because it will move).
- If no path to food exists, choose any non-lethal adjacent move, preferring the one with the largest reachable free area (flood-fill count) so the snake avoids trapping itself.
- When possible, avoid moving into a cell orthogonally adjacent to the opponent's head to reduce head-on collisions.
- AI must be deterministic enough to look smooth (no random jitter when a clear path exists).

== SCREENS (overlays positioned over the canvas, semi-transparent dark) ==
- START MENU shown on load: big "SNAKE" title, three mode buttons ("1 · Human vs Human", "2 · CPU vs Human", "3 · CPU vs CPU") with a one-line description each, and a controls legend (Player 1 arrows, Player 2 WASD, CPU hunts food automatically).
- GAME OVER screen: result line appropriate to the mode ("Player 1 Wins!", "Player 2 Wins!", "CPU Wins!", "Draw!"), final scores of both snakes, and the hint "Press R to play again · M for menu".

== CODE QUALITY ==
- Clean, commented, well-structured vanilla JS: small set of named functions (init/reset, spawnFood, step/update, cpuMove with BFS + flood fill, draw/render, input handlers, screen show/hide). No frameworks. Reasonable initial snake placement (e.g., Snake 1 starting left side heading right, Snake 2 right side heading left, length 3 each).","path":"snake_openrouter-moonshotai-kimi-k3_01.html"}
